designVerdict: SELECTED - the two channel switches (Q1, Q2), driven by the LM5069.
notes: Replaces the P-channel TM40P06D (C7422850). N-channel because the LM5069 charge pump drives the gate above the source, which is what made the high-side gate network unnecessary.
100 V against the SMAJ36CA 58.1 V clamp is 1.72x, where the 60 V P-FET sat at 1.03x - a margin this design twice called uncomfortable and twice failed to fix.
Rds(on) 9.5 mOhm max at Vgs 10 V (p.1), roughly 13.3 mOhm at Tj 100 C, so 0.079 W at the 2.43 A channel current. Lower loss AND higher voltage than the 60 V P-FET, at $0.39 against $0.40.

Publishes a real SOA family (Fig. 12 p.4) with 10 us / 100 us / 1 ms / 10 ms / DC curves. There is no 100 ms curve, so the 132 ms ramp is bounded by the DC line: roughly 0.6 A at Vds 36 V, about 21 W, against the 18 W power limit. The TM40P06D had only a DC line and no family at all, which is why its SOA was unverifiable.
RthJA 50 C/W on 1 in2 of 2 oz copper (p.1 note 2), so about 2.5 W at 25 C ambient. Steady state is not the binding constraint; the 18 W ramp is, and that is transient.
Datasheet lists "PD Charger V-BUS" as a typical application.
